searchText: There would need to be a slashed validator that is eligible to become a proposer. Likely someone will need to slash itself in the middle of upgrade rollout when there is no majority on either side of the upgrade I am not trying to say that uncoordinated upgrade is completely safe, but the probability of a split to happen is much lower than usually, and I have been convinced that we should do this in coordination This is not so unlikely ifv there's some large slashing. And in those circumstances the very last place we want to be is on a split. My first impression about these changes is that it's part of those things that would have been nice to know beforehand in 2020. Given the status quo I believe it's probably better to leave it as is, and if we get to a point that the percentage of slashed validators bug the throughput of the network, then we can come back and change this I agree, testing and coordination efforts with no tangible outcome make this change unlikely to happen Merry Christmas everyone! 🎉 https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3177 > Eliminate requirement to maintain and distribute deposit contract snapshots (EIP-4881).
